name: Thanksgiving
seo_title: Thanksgiving Charcuterie Board Ideas: 8 Easy Boards (+ Turkey Board)
description: 8 Thanksgiving charcuterie board ideas: a turkey-shaped board, an easy board under $40, Friendsgiving, a pie board, baked brie, a vegan fall board and more, plus how much to buy for 6 to 20 guests.
answer: A Thanksgiving charcuterie board should hold guests over, not fill them up: keep it light before dinner, lean on fall flavors (sharp cheddar, apple, pear, cranberry, pecans, maple) and serve it about an hour before the turkey. For a crowd, build the turkey-shaped board; for a small table, an easy board for under $40 does the job.

ideas.title: The Turkey-Shaped Board
ideas.text: A fan of crackers, salami and sliced cheese makes the tail; a round of Brie or a pear makes the body; a candied pecan and a pretzel make the face. Kids love it and it photographs well.

ideas.title: The Easy Board Under $40
ideas.text: One sharp cheddar, one soft cheese, one salami, apples and grapes, a sleeve of crackers and a jar of fig jam. Five minutes to build.

ideas.title: The Friendsgiving Potluck Anchor
ideas.text: A big board that goes on the table first so guests have something while the dishes arrive: two cheeses, two meats, roasted nuts, apple butter and plenty of crackers.

ideas.title: The Fall Harvest Board
ideas.text: Every fall flavor in one place: apples, pears, figs, maple and spiced nuts next to sharp and creamy cheeses. It works for the whole season, not just the day itself.

ideas.title: The Thanksgiving Pie Board
ideas.text: Slices of three or four pies on one board with whipped cream, caramel and a sharp cheddar for the apple pie. It replaces the crowded pie table and lets everyone try a little of each.
ideas.on_it: Pumpkin, pecan and apple pie slices · whipped cream · caramel sauce · sharp cheddar · candied pecans · berries

ideas.title: The Baked Brie Centerpiece
ideas.text: One wheel of brie, baked until it slumps and topped with cranberry sauce, pecans and maple, in the middle of a simple board. Bake it in the morning before the turkey takes over the oven, or right before guests arrive.
ideas.on_it: Brie · cranberry sauce · pecans · maple syrup · sliced baguette · apples · crackers

ideas.title: The Holiday Cheese Ball Board
ideas.text: A cheese ball rolled in pecans and cranberries, made two days ahead, surrounded by crackers, apples and celery. The easiest board on this page on the day itself.
ideas.on_it: Cheese ball rolled in pecans and dried cranberries · crackers · apple slices · celery · pretzel crisps

ideas.title: The Vegan Fall Harvest Board
ideas.text: Cashew cheese, a pumpkin seed dip, roasted delicata squash and candied pecans. Put it out next to the regular board so nobody has to ask what they can eat.

shapes.name: Turkey Board
steps: Place a round of Brie or a halved pear low in the center as the body.
Fan rows of crackers, salami, cheese slices and apple slices above it in a half circle for the tail.
Give it a face: a candied pecan beak and two pretzel or olive eyes.

shapes.name: Cornucopia Board
steps: Lay a curved line of breadsticks or a folded tortilla horn at one corner.
Spill grapes, figs, apples and nuts out of the open end across the board.
Tuck cheese and meat into the flow so it looks like a harvest spilling out.

shapes.name: Leaf Garland Board
steps: Run a diagonal line of cheese cut with a leaf-shaped cookie cutter across the board.
Line both sides with folded salami and prosciutto.
Fill the corners with pears, pecans and crackers.

plan.what: Order specialty cheese, and buy nuts, jams and crackers (they keep).
Buy fresh fruit, cheese and meat. Make or buy the dips.
Slice hard cheeses and fold meats; cover and chill. The oven belongs to the turkey, so do anything warm (baked Brie) now.
Take cheese out of the fridge. Build the board.
Put the board out. Take it away when the turkey comes out so nobody fills up.

faq.q: Should you serve charcuterie before Thanksgiving dinner?
faq.a: Yes. Stick to the before-a-meal amount, about 2 oz each of cheese and meat per guest, set it out about an hour before dinner, and lean on fruit, nuts and pickles so it holds people over without spoiling the meal.

faq.q: How do you make a turkey-shaped charcuterie board?
faq.a: Place a round of Brie or a pear low in the center as the body, fan crackers, salami and cheese above it as the tail, and use a pecan and two pretzels for the face.

faq.q: What cheeses go best on a Thanksgiving board?
faq.a: A sharp aged cheddar, a creamy Brie and one wildcard like smoked Gouda or a cranberry goat cheese. They all pair with apples, pears and cranberry.

faq.q: Can I make a Thanksgiving charcuterie board the day before?
faq.a: Prep the day before, build on the day. Slice hard cheeses and fold meats the night before, keep them covered in the fridge, and assemble on the board the day of.

faq.q: What goes on a Friendsgiving charcuterie board?
faq.a: Two cheeses, two meats, roasted nuts, apple butter or fig jam, fruit and lots of crackers. Make it big enough for 16 so it feeds people while the potluck dishes arrive.

faq.q: How much charcuterie do I need for Thanksgiving?
faq.a: Before dinner, plan about 2 oz of cheese, 2 oz of meat and 6–8 crackers per guest. For 12 guests that's about 1.5 lb of cheese and 1.5 lb of meat. The table above gives amounts for 6 to 20 guests.

faq.q: What is a Thanksgiving pie board?
faq.a: A dessert board with slices of several pies, plus whipped cream, caramel, berries and a sharp cheddar. It replaces a crowded pie table and lets everyone try a little of each.

faq.q: What's a good vegan Thanksgiving charcuterie board?
faq.a: Cashew cheese, a pumpkin seed dip, roasted squash, apples, candied pecans, dried cranberries and fig jam. The Vegan Fall Harvest Board above has the full list.

faq.q: How much does a Thanksgiving charcuterie board cost?
faq.a: Before a meal, plan about $3 to $5 per guest on a budget and $5 to $8 for a standard board, so roughly $35 to $60 or $60 to $95 for 12 guests. Splurge cheeses and meats run $12 or more per guest. Store and region change the total.

mistakes.text: Before a turkey dinner, 2 oz each of cheese and meat per guest is plenty. A board sized for a party fills people up before the meal.
Set it out about an hour before dinner and clear it when the turkey comes out. A board that sits all afternoon gets picked over and warm.

mistakes.lead: Fighting the turkey for the oven.
mistakes.text: Anything warm, like baked brie, gets baked in the morning or while the turkey rests. Plan the board around the oven, not the other way around.

mistakes.lead: Forgetting the guests who skip meat or dairy.
mistakes.text: One small vegan or vegetarian board, or a clearly labeled section, saves a lot of questions at the table.

ahead: Up to 3 days: a cheese ball, wrapped tightly and chilled
2 days: dips and spreads; toasted or candied nuts in an airtight jar
The night before: slice firm cheeses and fold the meats, then cover and chill
The night before: wash and dry the grapes
last: Bake any warm brie before the turkey takes the oven
Slice apples and pears last so they don't brown
Take soft cheese out only 20 to 30 minutes ahead
Add crackers just before the board goes out
